C-REMOVE-SESSION-ORCHESTRATION-PROFILES.IntentSummary: Remove the four session-wide orchestration profiles from every public surface and runtime request path while preserving subagents and tracked workflows. Families with a recorded profile keep their previously resolved tail policy and workflow-protocol variant as a documented transition boundary and never receive the new stable controller default; families without a recorded profile receive one short controller default inside the stable managed controller system prompt, no tail injection, and no profile-specific workflow protocol. Legacy vvoc.json documents with root or per-preset orchestration sections migrate through one explicit host-gated vvoc sync step with a timestamped backup and a change report; strict parsing elsewhere fails loudly and the canonical schema stays v3. Graph, verification projections, README, and tests are synchronized.

MustContain.Text: Follow the concrete work policy supplied for this session

MustPassCommand.Command: bun test src/lib/orchestration.test.ts src/lib/vvoc-config.test.ts src/commands/config-validate.test.ts src/commands/preset.test.ts src/commands/session.test.ts src/commands/status.test.ts src/commands/completion.test.ts src/tui/settings/plugin.test.ts

PlanningNotes.Note: Transition model: the recorded profile in the session-owned family settings record is the only boundary marker. Families with a recorded profile keep the existing tail policy text and workflow-protocol variant and are excluded from the new short default; families without a recorded profile get no tail injection, no profile-specific workflow protocol, and the single short default from the stable controller system prompt. Every explicit settings rewrite (any vvoc session set change or /vv-settings action, including pull-defaults) drops the profile and completes the transition; a family whose root no longer resolves through lineage has ended.

Short default placement: the new stable section <work_policy_default> lives in templates/agents/vv-controller.md and is projected by system-context-injection as an additional system part for families without a recorded profile, so it stays inside the cached stable prefix and never enters user messages.

Legacy policies stay internal: src/lib/orchestration.ts keeps ORCHESTRATION_PROFILE_NAMES, the profile type, strict parse for decoding recorded values, and the four frozen policy texts; only the config-facing constructors and the absent-section default are removed, so no public CLI or config surface remains.

Migration semantics: a new M-CLI-CONFIG helper runs inside vvoc sync after the host-window gate and before readVvocConfig, for project and global vvoc.json; it removes only root and per-preset orchestration keys via formatting-preserving edits, writes <path>.vvoc-backup-<timestamp>, reports removed sections and paths, leaves invalid JSON untouched so strict parsing fails loudly, and is idempotent. The canonical schema version stays v3 because orchestration was optional.

Workflow behavior: tool registration, root gating, acceptance, review, blocker, and recovery enforcement are untouched; only the profile-selected guidance injection becomes conditional on a recorded profile. Ordinary requests open no work item because work_item_open remains an explicit tool call.

Durable cleanup: M-CLI-ORCHESTRATION and V-M-CLI-ORCHESTRATION are removed from both indexes and routed documents; every surviving anchor's purpose and verification scenario drops the profile choice while describing the transition behavior and the sync migration.

GRACE lifecycle commands (grace lint, grace status, assertion phases) run externally around execution and never inside plan commands; plan status moves to approved only after the review round completes and the user-approved execution flow starts.

T-001.Title: Make the recorded profile optional and resolve policy from it in both plugins.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src/lib/orchestration.ts exposes policyForRecordedProfile(profile) returning the frozen legacy policy for a recorded profile and undefined for an absent one, while the existing config-facing constructors stay in place for the later surface-removal task.
FamilySettings.profile is optional; decodeFamilySettings accepts an absent profile and still fails soft on an invalid present value; describeFamilySettings prints the profile only when it is present.
projectFamilyConfig overrides roles and plugin toggles only and never fabricates an orchestration section.

system-context-injection resolves the tail policy only from a recorded profile and appends no tail for a record without one; the workflow plugin resolves policy the same way and injects guidance only when a recorded profile exists; tool registration and root gating are unchanged.
isMeaningfulFamilySettingsView accepts a settings record without a profile and still rejects incomplete records; the allowlisted projection exposes a profile only when recorded.
Session-settings, context-inspection, both plugin suites, and model-roles integration tests pass with records that both carry and omit a profile.

T-002.Title: Remove orchestration from the canonical config, presets, CLI, and session-settings write paths.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: VvocConfig, the JSON schema (root and per-preset), config seeding, normalization, and preset overrides no longer contain or accept orchestration; a document with an orchestration section fails strict v3 validation loudly and no version bump occurs.
Built-in presets declare roles only; vvoc preset applies and reports roles without any profile notion.
The vvoc orchestration command and its test are deleted and the command is unregistered; CLI help, status output, inspection, and bash/zsh/fish completions expose no orchestration or profile choice.

vvoc session set has no profile action and the TUI /vv-settings command offers no profile action; preset, role, plugin toggle, and pull-defaults still work; pull-defaults rewrites the family record without a profile.

settingsFromConfig births records without a profile; src/lib/orchestration.ts no longer exports createOrchestrationConfig, resolveOrchestrationPolicy, or the absent-section default; no source file references the removed symbols.
All command, config, orchestration, TUI, and opencode seeding tests pass on the updated behavior.

Verification.Command: bun test src/lib/orchestration.test.ts src/lib/vvoc-config.test.ts src/commands/config-validate.test.ts src/commands/preset.test.ts src/commands/session.test.ts src/commands/status.test.ts src/commands/completion.test.ts src/tui/settings/plugin.test.ts src/lib/opencode.test.ts

T-003.Title: Add the stable short controller default and retire profile wording from managed skills.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: templates/agents/vv-controller.md carries exactly one <work_policy_default> section stating that ordinary implementation stays in the current session unless the user requests delegation or a selected plan calls for it, bounded search assistance does not select an execution mode, and independent review happens only when explicitly requested or materially useful; the existing sections keep their meaning.

guidance.ts requires exactly one work-policy-default section and exposes it separately from the seven controller sections; a missing or duplicated section throws explicitly, and the shared-primary projection stays free of controller-only instructions.

system-context-injection appends the default fragment to system parts only for families without a recorded profile and never to user messages; families with a recorded profile keep the legacy tail and receive no default fragment.

templates/skills/vv-execute/SKILL.md no longer references an active orchestration profile; execution intent comes from the plan, the user, or a selected execution mode without any session-wide policy lookup.
Managed agent and managed skill suites plus the system-context-injection suite pass with the new template and skill text.

T-004.Title: Add the explicit host-gated legacy orchestration migration to vvoc sync.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A new M-CLI-CONFIG helper removes root and per-preset orchestration keys from project and global vvoc.json using formatting-preserving edits, leaves every other key and value verbatim, and is a no-op on documents without those keys.
Each migrated document gets a timestamped sibling backup named <path>.vvoc-backup-<timestamp> before the write, and the command reports each migrated path with the removed sections.

vvoc sync runs the migration after the host-window gate and before the strict vvoc config read; invalid JSON is left untouched so the subsequent strict parse fails loudly, and a second run changes nothing.
Unit tests cover root-only, preset-only, mixed, absent, invalid-JSON, backup-creation, and idempotent second-run cases through isolated temp directories; the sync suite passes.

T-005.Title: Synchronize GRACE durable state and README with the removed profile surface.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: M-CLI-ORCHESTRATION and V-M-CLI-ORCHESTRATION are removed from the graph and verification indexes and routed documents, and no anchor or reference points at them.

Every surviving affected module purpose/scope and verification scenario describes the retired profile surface, the recorded-profile transition boundary, the sync migration, and the stable short default instead of the removed profile choice; test file and command lists match the actual suites.

README drops the orchestration-profile section, the orchestration command rows, the preset-to-profile table, and every claim that profiles select behavior; it documents the Controller execution default, the Legacy orchestration migration step, and the recorded-profile transition boundary, and no longer claims a seven-section controller prompt.
bun run check (including the GRACE markup gate) and bun run build pass on the finished tree.
